hypothesis: The best parent c021 (decay<=0.5, ignore_net_degree halved, adam scheme) is robust; combining it with a modest, bounded per-net weight cap applied only to the effective weight passed to the C++ update (via the existing `max_net_weight` argument) will spread timing weight across more moderately-critical nets and reduce TNS without the systematic failures seen when the cap was set too tight externally.
analysis: The hypothesis held: the bounded per-net cap improved all three cases with no invalid runs. dWNS rose 27.5–31.8% and dTNS 17.5–30.7%, with overflow ~100–139. The mechanism is plausible—capping effective weight spreads timing pressure to moderately-critical nets, reducing TNS without the systematic failures of a tight external cap. Next step: sweep the cap value (e.g., 0.5×, 1×, 2× current) to confirm the bounded region is robust and locate the onset of the earlier failure mode.
